For long-stop dates, recompute by adding the stated period to the agreement date and cross-check against expected fulfilment dates. Flag discrepancies, ambiguities in trigger events, or business day definitions. Verify calculations against the document's stated date and flag mismatches.

For every date-based obligation, deadline, or time-bound provision: (1) recompute the expiry date by adding the stated duration to the anchor date; (2) explicitly state the duration, specific calendar expiry date, day of the week, business day status, and days remaining from the review date; (3) apply the document's Business Day definition to adjust deadlines falling on weekends/holidays, using a date calculator to confirm; (4) state the final deadline after adjustment; (5) for conditional deadlines, specify the trigger event, stated deadline, business day adjustment, and final deadline; (6) for rolling deadlines, clarify the trigger event and calculate the deadline for sample scenarios. For long-stop dates, recompute by adding the stated period to the agreement date. Directly compute days remaining from the deliverable date to the expiry date using a date calculator, cross-checking arithmetic. Flag discrepancies, ambiguities in trigger events, or business day definitions. Verify calculations against the document's stated date and flag mismatches.

For every date-based obligation, deadline, or time-bound provision: (1) recompute the expiry date by adding the stated duration to the anchor date using inclusive counting unless the document specifies exclusive counting; (2) explicitly state the duration, specific calendar expiry date, day of the week, business day status, and days remaining from the review date; (3) apply the document's Business Day definition (or note its absence as a critical risk) to adjust deadlines falling on weekends/holidays; (4) state the final deadline after adjustment, verifying the adjusted date complies with the Business Day definition using a date calculator; (5) for conditional deadlines, specify the trigger event, stated deadline, business day adjustment, and final deadline; (6) for rolling deadlines, clarify the trigger event and calculate the deadline for sample scenarios; (7) for long-stop dates, recompute by adding the stated period to the agreement date and cross-check against expected fulfilment dates. Verify date arithmetic by reversing the computation (e.g., subtracting the duration from the expiry date to recover the anchor date). Flag ambiguities in trigger events, missing Business Day definitions, or discrepancies in date calculations. Never apply a default Business Day definition without client confirmation.

For every time-bound provision (e.g., claim notification periods, escrow deadlines, notice periods): (1) explicitly state whether it is a fixed deadline (e.g., 'before [date]') or a rolling period (e.g., 'within X days of awareness'); (2) cross-check the exact wording of the governing clause to avoid misinterpretation; (3) document the trigger event, specific calendar expiry date, day of the week, business day status, days remaining from the deliverable date, calculation method, and tool used for verification; (4) apply the document's Business Day definition (or a default standard like 'days excluding weekends and public holidays') to adjust deadlines falling on non-Business Days; (5) for escrow agreements, create a timeline showing the trigger event, claim notification deadline, escrow release date, and legal consequence of missing each deadline; (6) verify the exact timing language (e.g., 'prior to', 'on or before') and flag ambiguities; (7) cross-check all related agreements for inconsistencies; (8) for inconsistent deadlines, prioritize the stricter (shorter) deadline to minimize client risk unless operational feasibility or market practice dictates otherwise, and document the practical implications of adopting each version; (9) for every pair of related time-bound provisions, create a side-by-side table comparing durations, trigger events, and legal consequences, and recommend harmonization to the stricter or most protective period; (10) recompute the expiry date by reversing the computation to verify accuracy; (11) document the rationale for the chosen deadline resolution.

For escrow agreements and every date-sensitive provision: (1) create a timeline showing the trigger event, claim notification deadline, escrow release date (unadjusted and adjusted for Business Days), days remaining from deliverable date, and legal consequence of missing each deadline; (2) explicitly state whether claims must be notified 'before', 'on', or 'by' the release date, and distinguish between general release and pending claim deadlines; (3) document the calculation method (inclusive/exclusive) and verification tool; (4) recompute deadlines for alternative trigger dates to verify consistency; (5) quote exact wording of governing clauses and flag ambiguities in timing language; (6) verify escrow release date by computing from the anchor date, checking day-of-week status, and applying Business Day adjustments; (7) include days remaining from deliverable date to each deadline, not just intermediate dates; (8) recompute the exact calendar date from the anchor date using a date calculator tool; (9) verify day-of-week, business day status, and alignment with document-stated dates; (10) recompute days remaining using at least two independent methods (e.g., manual count, date tool) and flag discrepancies exceeding one day; (11) document whether calculations are inclusive/exclusive of start/end dates; (12) cross-check deadlines across all transaction documents and flag inconsistencies; (13) for Business Day adjustments, explicitly state the original deadline, adjusted deadline, and rationale (e.g., 'next business day'); (14) use the deliverable date as the anchor for all days-remaining computations; (15) reverse-compute durations to verify accuracy; (16) for long-stop periods, recompute the expiry date from the signing date and cross-check against stated dates; (17) for provisions stating both a duration and specific date, treat the computed date as authoritative unless the document explicitly states otherwise; (18) flag discrepancies between computed and stated deadlines as high-risk inconsistencies; (19) ensure claim notification deadlines precede adjusted escrow release dates and document buffer periods.

top_helpful_lessons.text: For every key finding, deadline, risk, obligation, material assertion, or omission, include: (1) a pinpoint citation to the document and exact clause/section number, verified by cross-referencing the document's table of contents or internal numbering (if the document lacks formal numbering, use descriptive headings or line ranges and explicitly note the absence), (2) a direct quote of the clause or section heading alongside the citation, (3) a direct quote or paraphrase of the relevant text, (4) recomputed figure/date if applicable, (5) risk rating (High/Medium/Low), (6) concrete recommended action with clear verb, and (7) the legal consequence of non-compliance. For omissions, use phrases like 'No provision addressing [Issue]' to document gaps. Ensure citations are exact and avoid paraphrasing that could alter legal effect.

Create a timeline of all critical dates in transaction documents. Use a consistent date calculation tool to verify durations, cross-check results, and note implications like weekends, holidays, or missing 'Business Day' definitions. Avoid manual counting for durations exceeding 30 days. For deadlines tied to future events, recompute exact dates from anchor dates rather than summarizing as 'prior to X'. Use a consistent anchor date (e.g., deliverable date) for comparability across multiple deadlines. Document the anchor date and calculation method in deliverables.

Start every deliverable with a 'Bottom line' section summarising: (1) the overall conclusion (proceed/pause/stop), (2) a prioritized list of the 2-3 most critical risks by severity and urgency, labeling the single most critical risk first, (3) the single most time-sensitive issue in plain language for non-legal stakeholders, explicitly labeled as 'Most Time-Sensitive Issue:' followed by a one-sentence action requirement (e.g., 'Conflicting notice periods must be harmonized immediately'), stating: (a) the specific risk, (b) days remaining from the deliverable date, (c) the legal consequence of inaction, (d) the required action, and (e) the responsible party, (4) the days remaining from the deliverable date for the time-sensitive issue, (5) the legal consequence of inaction, and (6) a clear directive for next steps (e.g., 'immediate investigation required'). For critical inconsistencies (e.g., conflicting deadlines), explicitly label them as high-risk issues requiring immediate harmonization and include a one-sentence recommended action. Prioritise risks by severity and urgency. Ensure this section precedes detailed analysis.

For every time-bound provision (e.g., deadlines, survival periods, notice periods, escrow, long-stop dates), state: (1) the duration, (2) the specific calendar expiry date, (3) whether it falls on a business day or weekend/holiday, (4) days remaining from the deliverable date, (5) business days remaining if relevant, (6) the day-of-week status, (7) the start date and calculation method, (8) the anchor date and timing language, (9) the legal consequence of non-compliance, (10) any adjustments under a 'Business Day' rule (original and adjusted dates), (11) a 'Final Result' subsection confirming compliance with the Business Day definition, adjusted deadline, computed days remaining, and legal consequence, and (12) whether the computed date or document-stated date governs, justifying the choice (treat computed dates as authoritative unless the document explicitly states otherwise). Include a dedicated 'Date Calculations Verification' subsection showing: anchor date, calculation method, step-by-step arithmetic, computed deadline, business day adjustment, final deadline, and days remaining. Bold adjusted deadlines as 'Final Adjusted Deadline'.

Assign a standardised risk rating (High/Medium/Low) to every issue, risk, or discrepancy based on potential legal, financial, or operational impact and likelihood. Include the rating alongside the issue description in all sections of the deliverable. Ensure every identified risk includes a concrete, actionable recommendation.

Before finalising any deadline or timeline analysis, verify: (1) all key obligations trace to specific clauses, (2) derived dates are independently recomputed and adjusted for business days using the document’s definition or a fallback standard, (3) deadlines falling on weekends/holidays are adjusted under the document's 'Business Day' definition or a default standard, documented in a 'Business Day Adjustments' table with original date, adjusted date, and rationale, (4) durations, expiry dates, and days remaining from the deliverable date are explicitly stated and precise, (5) every deadline includes the specific calendar date, day-of-week status, Business Day adjustment (if applicable), adjusted deadline, days remaining from the deliverable date, and pinpoint citation, (6) all date-based obligations are expressed as both durations and specific calendar dates, (7) the number of days remaining from the deliverable date to each deadline is recomputed using at least two independent methods (e.g., manual count, date calculator), (8) all time-bound provisions are cross-checked across related documents for inconsistencies, (9) critical path conflicts and misalignments with third-party deadlines are flagged, (10) condition precedent deadlines are cross-checked against long-stop dates and extensions recommended for conflicts, (11) every computed deadline includes the calculation method, anchor date, and cross-check against a date calculator tool, (12) discrepancies exceeding one day are flagged as high-risk errors, (13) days-remaining calculations are computed from the deliverable date, not intermediate anchor dates, and cross-checked for accuracy, (14) for every date-sensitive provision, recompute the expiry date from the trigger event and treat computed dates as authoritative unless the document explicitly states otherwise. Include a 'Date Calculations Verification' subsection showing anchor date, calculation method, step-by-step arithmetic, computed deadline, and cross-checked days remaining. Bold final adjusted figures.

For every identified risk, issue, undisclosed liability, warranty breach, critical gap, or material risk, include a concrete recommended action tailored to the client's position. Specify: (1) the action verb using precise legal terminology, (2) the document/clause to be amended, (3) the responsible party, (4) deadline (if applicable), (5) status (obtained/outstanding), (6) whether it is 'required for closing', (7) the legal consequence of non-compliance, and (8) the financial exposure or impact on the client. Quantify the financial exposure where possible. Prioritize specific indemnities or price adjustments over generic remedies. For liability mechanisms, include a 'Liability Mechanics' subsection with: current position, proposed mitigation options, worked examples, and financial impact on the client. For risks involving third-party actions, frame recommendations as concrete conditions precedent (e.g., 'obtain written consent') tied to the closing timeline. For gaps (e.g., missing IP assignments), include a 'Recommended Action' subsection specifying the concrete step, responsible party, deadline, and legal consequence of inaction.

Before finalising any deliverable, verify that every numerical figure (e.g., caps, percentages, claim amounts, escrow amounts, purchase price adjustments) is recomputed step-by-step and cross-checked against source documents. Include arithmetic steps, base figures, derived values, and comparisons with stated figures. For financial discrepancies, include: (1) step-by-step arithmetic, (2) base figures, (3) computed vs. stated values, (4) absolute/relative discrepancy, (5) percentage variance, (6) implied base figures from reverse computation, (7) pinpoint citation, (8) risk rating, and (9) legal consequence and recommended amendment text for high-risk errors. Bold final adjusted amounts. Use a table format for financial calculations to list components and their impact. Flag discrepancies exceeding 0.5% of the base figure as high-risk errors. Reverse-compute implied base figures (e.g., implied EBITDA, working capital, purchase price, percentages) from stated adjustments and compare to source documents. Include a 'Reverse Computation Check' subsection in financial analyses. Ensure all derived figures are independently recomputed using at least two methods, include practical implications for the client, and match step-by-step computations. Cross-check all financial figures against the purchase price currency and recompute implied amounts in alternative currencies if applicable. Verify financial adjustments are correctly classified as deductions from or additions to the purchase price, and cross-check against the agreement’s definitions.

For ambiguous, inconsistent, or undefined terms: (1) create a side-by-side table comparing alternative interpretations (narrow vs. broad), legal/commercial effects, risks to the client, and recommended actions; (2) apply a consistent framework: quote exact wording, list alternative interpretations, document legal/commercial effects, assess risks, recommend resolution, and justify the choice; (3) document the legal test for enforceability and apply it to deviations; (4) include direct quotes from clauses and pinpoint citations; (5) benchmark against jurisdictional standards or market practice; (6) for restrictive covenants, compare duration, scope, and geographic reach against norms; (7) for undefined terms (e.g., 'Business Day'), document at least two plausible interpretations, their legal/commercial effects, and recommend a default definition aligned with client interests; (8) cross-check ancillary documents and disclosure letters for inconsistencies; (9) flag missing clauses or undisclosed provisions as critical gaps and recommend remedial actions; (10) for ambiguous provisions, apply a two-step framework: list all plausible interpretations with direct quotes and document the legal/commercial effect of each; (11) for conflicting notice periods or deadlines, create a comparison table with columns for: document, clause, duration, trigger event, legal consequence of missing the deadline, risk to client, and recommended harmonization; (12) for undisclosed liabilities or contradictory evidence, create a side-by-side comparison table with columns for warranty statement, disclosure letter statement, contradictory evidence, discrepancy analysis, legal consequence, and recommended remedial action; (13) quantify financial exposure and propose risk mitigation strategies (e.g., specific indemnity or escrow holdback).

Include a dedicated 'Conditions Precedent & Third-Party Actions' section listing all required approvals, consents, third-party actions (e.g., assignments, change-of-control consents), or conditions precedent. For each item, state: (1) counterparty name, (2) document source and pinpoint citation, (3) whether it has been validly obtained, (4) its current status (obtained/outstanding/invalid), (5) responsible parties, (6) associated risks of proceeding without it, (7) whether it is a condition precedent to closing, (8) label each as 'Required for Closing' in bold if its absence poses a high risk, (9) tie each to the closing timeline with a specific deadline, (10) distinguish between 'recommendations' and 'required actions', (11) include a concrete remedial action (e.g., 'obtain written consent') with responsible party and deadline for high-risk items, and (12) add a 'Deadline Conflicts' column flagging misalignment with long-stop dates or closing dates (label as 'High Risk'). For change-of-control provisions, explicitly list third-party consent as a required condition precedent. For every third-party action, state the legal test for enforceability (e.g., written assignment requirement for IP) and whether the current arrangement meets this standard. Include a 'Critical Path Conflicts' subsection listing timing conflicts between deadlines, third-party actions, or regulatory approvals, stating: (1) legal consequence, (2) days remaining from the deliverable date, (3) responsible parties, (4) risk rating (High/Medium/Low), and (5) recommended remedial actions.
